# The cache warm and the content-addressed package: the half of CI that needs
# repository writes. odu (github.com/juspay/odu) runs the checks themselves —
# the justfile recipe tagged [metadata("ci")] and its dependency graph — and
# posts one commit status per (recipe × platform). This workflow is what pushes
# the OSS cache and the `ca-index` branch, because ATTIC_TOKEN lives here, so
# `just protect` keeps its contexts required on main beside odu's.
name: Cache

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # A manual warm: a dispatch pushes what it builds to the cache and publishes
  # its `<rev>/<system>/…` entries. It writes no `latest/` entry, which moves
  # only on a push to main. Its `build (…)` and `publish (…)` contexts are
  # required on main, so dispatch on a commit that can land there.
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: cache-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The two systems odu has lanes for: ubuntu-latest is x86_64-linux and
        # macos-latest is arm64 (aarch64-darwin). aarch64-linux is not warmed.
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    env:
      ATTIC_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}
      # This job pushes what it builds when the run may write the cache: a main
      # push, a dispatch, or a same-repository pull request.
      PUSH_CACHE: >-
        ${{
          (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') ||
          github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
          (github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
           github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository)
        }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - uses: cachix/install-nix-action@13d8dd58da0234aa297dedd986986ccb8e7f3e24 # v31
        with:
          github_access_token: ${{ github.token }}
          # No release is pinned here: the one line that has to be a particular
          # Nix is the publisher's — the `publish` job's action installs 2.34.8
          # itself, because 2.35 hashes a self-referential NAR differently and
          # publisher and consumer must agree. This job builds and pushes signed
          # paths, which any line takes.
          #
          # Trust the project cache so builds pull from it (warms nix run /
          # nix develop on both platforms) instead of rebuilding.
          extra_nix_config: |
            extra-substituters = https://cache.nixos.asia/oss
            extra-trusted-public-keys = oss:KO872wNJkCDgmGN3xy9dT89WAhvv13EiKncTtHDItVU=

      - name: Check the cache config matches lib/cache.nix
        run: python3 .github/scripts/check-cache-config.py

      - name: Require cache token
        if: env.PUSH_CACHE == 'true'
        run: |
          if [ -z "$ATTIC_TOKEN" ]; then
            echo "::error::ATTIC_TOKEN must be set to push builds to the OSS cache."
            exit 1
          fi

      # The cache lets users and CI fetch source-built harnesses,
      # so a missing token is an error, not a skip.
      - uses: ryanccn/attic-action@5635a15ef0c5462194ffbd05d1daeddc74625c3a # v0.5.0
        if: env.PUSH_CACHE == 'true'
        with:
          endpoint: https://cache.nixos.asia
          cache: oss
          token: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}

      # odu runs the same two recipes (`flake`, `picker`) as its own nodes; they
      # are here because a push is what warms the cache for everybody else.
      - name: Build all flake outputs
        run: |
          nix build github:srid/devour-flake -L --no-link \
            --override-input flake .

      - name: Build the picker
        # The picker depends on every launcher, so this builds them all.
        run: |
          nix build --print-build-logs .#default

  # The content-addressed package and the index that names it, through the
  # publisher `@kolu/surface` and this distribution now share
  # (juspay/kolu#2294). The action installs the Nix it rewrites with, rewrites
  # the package, runs a program out of the rewrite, pushes the closure, reads
  # it back from the cache into a fresh store, and writes
  # `<rev>/<system>/<attribute>.json` — plus `latest/` on a push to main — to
  # the index `binary-cache.json` names (kept equal to lib/ca-index.nix). The
  # attribute is the one package's: `default` (src/update/ca-index.ts
  # `ATTRIBUTE`).
  #
  # Its own job, after the warm: the action's Nix has to be this job's only
  # Nix, and the signed closures `build` just pushed are what this job's builds
  # then substitute instead of compiling.
  publish:
    needs: build
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Both systems publish: Linux a content-addressed rewrite, macOS the
        # signed package alone (a rewritten Mach-O is killed on arm64 macOS).
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # This job pushes the content-addressed index, a branch of this repository.
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Read the nixpkgs the action installs attic from
        id: attic
        # attic-client comes from the nixpkgs this repository pins, never an
        # unpinned ref resolved at run time. Read without Nix, which this job
        # has none of until the action below installs the only one it uses.
        run: |
          set -eu
          locked=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("flake.lock"))["nodes"]["nixpkgs"]["locked"]["rev"])')
          echo "nixpkgs=github:NixOS/nixpkgs/$locked" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Read the package this publishes
        id: package
        # The one package per system, and — until 2026-11-14, thirty days after
        # the one-package release — the same package under the attribute the
        # profile-keyed index published it as: an installed updater polls
        # `<rev>/<system>/vanilla.json` until it is replaced by one that reads
        # `<rev>/<system>/default.json`, and that PR removes this alias and the
        # second installable and smoke line here.
        run: |
          set -eu
          echo "installables=.#default .#vanilla" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          { echo "smoke<<PACKAGES"
            printf 'default=bin/claude --version\nvanilla=bin/claude --version\n'
            echo "PACKAGES"; } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: juspay/kolu/.github/actions/publish-closure@5b14790a4eb9c383dfd7fa247bbff1af60f9eb92 # juspay/kolu#2294, on master
        with:
          installables: ${{ steps.package.outputs.installables }}
          # Where the package goes and where its index is written: the
          # declaration this repository checks in, because no Nix exists in
          # this job until the action installs the one it rewrites with.
          # check-cache-config.py keeps that file equal to lib/cache.nix and
          # lib/ca-index.nix, in the job that already runs it.
          sidecar: binary-cache.json
          # No `rev`: the action keys each entry by the commit being published —
          # on a pull request its head, never the merge commit GitHub makes for
          # the run — which its own action.yml states once.
          latest: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
          smoke: ${{ steps.package.outputs.smoke }}
          attic-nixpkgs: ${{ steps.attic.outputs.nixpkgs }}
          attic-token: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}
The plugin-relative working directory of the explicit-cwd server.

"""A stub of the content-addressed index: one port answers with the entry a test
wrote, the other refuses with 404, so a test can drive a published revision, an
unpublished one, and an entry that names the signed package alone (which is what
a darwin system gets).

Serves TLS: the updater fetches only an https base, so the stub has to be one
— a self-signed certificate the test points the updater's trust at
(NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS)."""
import http.server
import ssl
import sys

status, port, certificate, key = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4]
entry = sys.argv[5]
# Where the server appends every path it was asked for, so a test can check
# which entry the updater fetched (`default.json`, or the attribute a config
# names instead).
requests = sys.argv[6] if len(sys.argv) > 6 else None


class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        if requests is not None:
            with open(requests, 'a') as log:
                log.write(self.path + '\n')
        body = open(entry, 'rb').read() if status == 200 else b''
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
        self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass


server = http.server.HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', port), Handler)
context = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
# A stub for a test, but with the floor a server should have: TLS 1.0 and 1.1
# are not versions to offer anyone.
context.minimum_version = ssl.TLSVersion.TLSv1_2
context.load_cert_chain(certificate, key)
server.socket = context.wrap_socket(server.socket, server_side=True)
server.serve_forever()

"""Read discovery from the real Claude launcher, without authentication or model calls."""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import sys

expected = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
home = Path.home()
# Where a launch's translations live: the adapter translates at launch, by
# content, under this root (src/plugin/launch.ts), never into the store.
translations = Path(os.environ.get('XDG_CACHE_HOME') or home / '.cache') / 'agent-distro' / 'plugins'
config_dir = home / 'relocated-claude'
config_dir.mkdir()
env = dict(os.environ, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=str(config_dir))
for key in ['LITELLM_API_KEY', 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', 'CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN']:
    env.pop(key, None)

settings = config_dir / 'settings.json'
settings.write_text('{"model":"sonnet","env":{"PERSONAL_SETTING":"keep"}}\n')
credentials = config_dir / '.credentials.json'
credentials.write_text('{}\n')
session = config_dir / 'projects' / 'keep.jsonl'
session.parent.mkdir()
session.write_text('session sentinel\n')
preserved = {path: path.read_bytes() for path in [settings, credentials, session]}


def run(*args, launcher='claude', plugins=None):
    # `plugins` is AGENT_DISTRO_PLUGINS for this launch only.
    extra = {} if plugins is None else {'AGENT_DISTRO_PLUGINS': plugins}
    return subprocess.run([launcher, *args], env=env | extra, text=True,
                          capture_output=True, timeout=60, check=True).stdout


def inventory(plugin, launcher='claude', plugins=None):
    # Claude's own inventory, rather than inspecting the translated files.
    details = run('plugin', 'details', plugin, launcher=launcher, plugins=plugins)
    # An MCP-only plugin prints `Skills (0)` with no names after it.
    match = re.search(r'^\s*Skills \((\d+)\)[ \t]*([^\n]*)', details, re.MULTILINE)
    assert match, details
    names = set(filter(None, match[2].split(', ')))
    assert len(names) == int(match[1]), details
    return names, details


def checkout(name, skill):
    """A plugin working copy outside the store, as a user edits one."""
    root = home / 'checkouts' / name
    (root / 'skills' / skill).mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / 'plugin.json').write_text(json.dumps({
        '$schema': 'https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json', 'name': name}))
    (root / 'skills' / skill / 'SKILL.md').write_text(f'---\nname: {skill}\ndescription: {skill}\n---\n')
    return str(root)

"""Read discovery from OpenCode without authentication or model calls."""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

expected = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
binary = 'opencode'
home = Path.home()
config_dir = home / '.config/opencode'
config_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
settings = config_dir / 'opencode.json'
# Upstream adds $schema to schema-less files when loading any configuration.
settings.write_text('{"$schema":"https://opencode.ai/config.json","username":"personal-user"}\n')
preserved = settings.read_bytes()
env = dict(os.environ, AGENT_DISTRO_SETTINGS='0', OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH='true',
           OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE='true', OPENCODE_PASSWORD='fixture')


def with_plugins(plugins):
    # AGENT_DISTRO_PLUGINS for one launch only.
    return env if plugins is None else env | {'AGENT_DISTRO_PLUGINS': plugins}


def run(*args, launcher=binary, plugins=None):
    # Upstream exits before large pipe writes drain; a file keeps the full JSON.
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile(mode='w+', encoding='utf-8') as output:
        result = subprocess.run([launcher, *args], env=with_plugins(plugins), text=True,
                                stdout=output, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, timeout=90)
        output.seek(0)
        stdout = output.read()
    assert result.returncode == 0, (stdout, result.stderr)
    return stdout


def config(launcher=binary, plugins=None):
    # The personal fixture and generated document have disjoint settings.
    return {key: value for entry in api('config', launcher, plugins) if entry['type'] == 'document'
            for key, value in entry['info'].items()}


def api(resource, launcher=binary, plugins=None):
    # The server reads the config; `api` only talks to it.
    with subprocess.Popen([launcher, 'serve', '--stdio', '--port', '0'], env=with_plugins(plugins),
                          stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True) as server:
        try:
            url = json.loads(server.stdout.readline())['url']
            def get(resource):
                return json.loads(run('api', '--server', url, 'GET', '/api/' + resource,
                                      '--header', 'x-opencode-directory:' + str(home), launcher=launcher))
            # Cold locations activate plugins asynchronously; this endpoint waits for activation.
            get('integration')
            for _ in range(60):
                result = get(resource)
                if resource != 'mcp' or all(s['status']['status'] != 'pending' for s in result['data']):
                    return result
                time.sleep(0.5)
            raise AssertionError(result)
        finally:
            server.stdin.close()
            server.wait(timeout=90)


def servers(resolved):
    mcp = resolved.get('mcp', {})
    return mcp.get('servers', {})


def skill_paths(resolved):
    return resolved['skills']


def check_inventory(launcher=binary):
    resolved = config(launcher)
    assert resolved['username'] == 'personal-user', resolved
    discovered = api('skill', launcher)['data']
    locations = [skill['path'] for skill in discovered]
    for plugin, names in expected.items():
        for name in names:
            assert any(location.endswith(f'/{plugin}/{name}/SKILL.md')
                       for location in locations), (plugin, name, discovered)
    for name, server in servers(resolved).items():
        assert server['type'] in ['local', 'remote'], (name, server)
    assert settings.read_bytes() == preserved
    return resolved


def checkout(name, skill):
    """A plugin working copy outside the store, as a user edits one."""
    root = home / 'checkouts' / name
    (root / 'skills' / skill).mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / 'plugin.json').write_text(json.dumps({
        '$schema': 'https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json', 'name': name}))
    (root / 'skills' / skill / 'SKILL.md').write_text(f'---\nname: {skill}\ndescription: {skill}\n---\n')
    return str(root)


def skill_locations(plugins=None):
    return [skill['path'] for skill in api('skill', plugins=plugins)['data']]

"""Probe the real OMP ACP session and process environment without model calls."""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

expected = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
expected_skills = {skill for skills in expected.values() for skill in skills}


def discover(launcher='omp', env=None, skills=None):
    want = expected_skills if skills is None else skills
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as cwd, tempfile.TemporaryFile(mode='w+') as output:
        process = subprocess.Popen([launcher, 'acp'], cwd=cwd, env=env,
                                   stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=output,
                                   stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
        try:
            process.stdin.write(json.dumps({'jsonrpc': '2.0', 'id': 1, 'method': 'initialize',
                'params': {'protocolVersion': 1, 'clientCapabilities': {'fs': {'readTextFile': False, 'writeTextFile': False}}}}) + '\n')
            process.stdin.flush()
            def wait_for_response(request_id):
                deadline = time.monotonic() + 120
                messages = []
                while time.monotonic() < deadline:
                    # Ignore a partial final line while the child is writing it.
                    data = os.pread(output.fileno(), os.fstat(output.fileno()).st_size, 0)
                    lines = data.splitlines(keepends=True)
                    messages = [json.loads(line) for line in lines
                                if line.endswith(b'\n') and line.strip()]
                    assert process.poll() is None, (process.returncode, messages)
                    responses = [m for m in messages if m.get('id') == request_id]
                    # OMP deliberately sends command discovery after session/new.
                    commands_ready = any(
                        m.get('method') == 'session/update' and
                        m.get('params', {}).get('update', {}).get('sessionUpdate') ==
                        'available_commands_update' for m in messages)
                    if responses and (request_id != 2 or commands_ready or
                                      'error' in responses[0]):
                        return messages
                    time.sleep(0.1)
                raise AssertionError(('ACP response timed out', request_id, messages))

            initialized = wait_for_response(1)
            assert any(m.get('id') == 1 and 'result' in m for m in initialized), initialized
            environ = Path(f'/proc/{process.pid}/environ').read_bytes().split(b'\0')
            process.stdin.write(json.dumps({'jsonrpc': '2.0', 'id': 2, 'method': 'session/new',
                'params': {'cwd': cwd, 'mcpServers': []}}) + '\n')
            process.stdin.flush()
            messages = wait_for_response(2)
            assert any(m.get('id') == 2 and 'result' in m for m in messages), messages
            found = set(re.findall(r'"name":\s*"skill:([^"]+)"', json.dumps(messages)))
            assert found == want, (found, want, messages)
            return environ
        finally:
            process.terminate()
            process.communicate(timeout=10)


def checkout(name, skill):
    """A plugin working copy outside the store, as a user edits one."""
    root = Path.home() / 'checkouts' / name
    (root / 'skills' / skill).mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / 'plugin.json').write_text(json.dumps({
        '$schema': 'https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json', 'name': name}))
    (root / 'skills' / skill / 'SKILL.md').write_text(f'---\nname: {skill}\ndescription: {skill}\n---\n')
    return str(root)

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import tomllib

expected = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
# A plugin whose name contains "." cannot be enabled with Codex's `-c` — its
# key splits at every dot, and a quoted key does not take — so the adapter
# registers its marketplace and leaves the plugin disabled, saying so. Every
# check over this support is about the plugins a launch does enable.
expected = {name: names for name, names in expected.items() if '.' not in name}
# A plugin gets a marketplace of its own, named after its cache key
# (src/harness/codex.ts), so all argv[2] can carry is the prefix they share;
# a check that needs a marketplace derives it from `codex plugin list --json`.
marketplace_prefix = sys.argv[2]
home = Path.home()
codex_home = home / 'relocated-codex'
codex_home.mkdir()
# Where Codex keeps its installs, and where the adapter keeps the translations
# it registers as marketplaces (src/plugin/launch.ts); neither is a store path.
install_cache = codex_home / 'plugins' / 'cache'
translations = Path(os.environ.get('XDG_CACHE_HOME') or home / '.cache') / 'agent-distro' / 'plugins'
env = dict(os.environ, CODEX_HOME=str(codex_home), AGENT_DISTRO_SETTINGS='0')
config = codex_home / 'config.toml'
config.write_text('# personal settings\nmodel = "my-model"\n[mcp_servers.personal]\ncommand = "true"\n')
auth = codex_home / 'auth.json'
auth.write_text('{"OPENAI_API_KEY":"test-api-key"}\n')
session = codex_home / 'sessions' / 'keep.jsonl'
session.parent.mkdir()
session.write_text('session sentinel\n')
skill = codex_home / 'skills' / 'personal' / 'SKILL.md'
skill.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
skill.write_text('---\nname: personal\ndescription: Personal skill\n---\n')


def with_plugins(plugins):
    # AGENT_DISTRO_PLUGINS for one launch only.
    return env if plugins is None else env | {'AGENT_DISTRO_PLUGINS': plugins}


def run(*args, launcher='codex', plugins=None, **kwargs):
    """One Codex run. A caller's `check=True` still raises, but with the
    command's own words: `subprocess`'s own error throws the stderr away, and
    that is the evidence a failing check needs."""
    check = kwargs.pop('check', False)
    result = subprocess.run([launcher, *args], env=with_plugins(plugins), text=True,
                            capture_output=True, timeout=60, **kwargs)
    if check:
        assert result.returncode == 0, (result.stdout, result.stderr)
    return result


def assert_kolu_server(servers):
    """The kolu plugin's server reaches Codex through a generated launcher.

    Codex starts a plugin's stdio servers in the plugin root — the spec's
    default, and a /nix/store path for a plugin from a flake reference, where
    `nix run github:…` cannot run — so the adapter installs a copy whose
    `mcp.json` names a launcher, which runs the plugin's own command in the
    directory Codex was launched in (doc/index.md).
    """
    server = servers['kolu']
    assert server['enabled'], server
    assert server['transport']['command'].endswith('bin/kolu-0-kolu'), server
    assert server['transport']['args'] == [], server
    # And it runs: the fixture answers an MCP initialize as kolu's server.
    launchers = list(codex_home.glob('plugins/cache/*/kolu/*/bin/kolu-0-kolu'))
    assert len(launchers) == 1, launchers
    launcher = launchers[0]
    started = subprocess.run([str(launcher)], text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=60,
                             input='{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18"}}\n')
    assert json.loads(started.stdout.splitlines()[0])['result']['serverInfo']['name'] == 'kolu-test', started


def upstream(*args):
    # A launcher with no profile: what Codex sees from config.toml alone.
    return subprocess.run(['codex-upstream', *args], env=env, text=True,
                          capture_output=True, timeout=60, check=True)


def installed_plugins(launcher='codex', plugins=None):
    """Codex's installed plugins during a launch, keyed by pluginId.

    A launch registers its marketplaces with `-c` and writes none of them, so
    only a launcher's own invocation lists them; codex-upstream lists nothing.
    """
    listing = run('plugin', 'list', '--json', launcher=launcher, plugins=plugins, check=True)
    return {plugin['pluginId']: plugin for plugin in json.loads(listing.stdout)['installed']}


def launched_plugins(launcher='codex', plugins=None):
    """The same, keyed by name: a launch registers each plugin once, under its
    own `agent-distro-` marketplace."""
    by_name = {}
    for plugin in installed_plugins(launcher, plugins).values():
        assert plugin['marketplaceName'].startswith(marketplace_prefix), plugin
        assert plugin['name'] not in by_name, (plugin, by_name)
        by_name[plugin['name']] = plugin
    return by_name


def marketplace_of(name, launcher='codex', plugins=None):
    """The marketplace a launch installs `name` under. It is named after the
    plugin's content, so it is the same for every launch of that content and
    another one once the plugin is rebuilt."""
    return launched_plugins(launcher, plugins)[name]['marketplaceName']


def plugin_id(name, launcher='codex', plugins=None):
    """`<name>@<marketplace>`, as Codex keys a plugin's own settings."""
    return launched_plugins(launcher, plugins)[name]['pluginId']


def marketplace_root(name, launcher='codex', plugins=None):
    """What Codex installed `name` from: the adapter's cached translation,
    holding the plugin under its own name."""
    root = launched_plugins(launcher, plugins)[name]['marketplaceSource']['source']
    assert root.startswith(str(translations) + '/'), (root, str(translations))
    return root


def installs():
    """The marketplace directories Codex has installed into."""
    return {entry.name for entry in install_cache.iterdir()} if install_cache.exists() else set()


def loaded_skills(launcher='codex', plugins=None):
    # No thread or model request: initialize, then ask the real app server for
    # its effective skills. A timeout also catches protocol changes in updates.
    process = subprocess.Popen([launcher, 'app-server'], env=with_plugins(plugins),
                               stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                               stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True)
    def request(request_id, method, params):
        process.stdin.write(json.dumps({'id': request_id, 'method': method, 'params': params}) + '\n')
        process.stdin.flush()
        for line in process.stdout:
            response = json.loads(line)
            if response.get('id') == request_id:
                assert 'error' not in response, response
                return response['result']
        raise AssertionError('Codex exited without answering ' + method)

    def timeout(*_):
        raise TimeoutError('Codex skill discovery timed out')

    signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, timeout)
    signal.alarm(60)
    try:
        request(1, 'initialize', {'clientInfo': {'name': 'ai-test', 'version': '1'},
                                  'capabilities': {'experimentalApi': True}})
        process.stdin.write('{"method":"initialized"}\n')
        process.stdin.flush()
        result = request(2, 'skills/list', {'cwds': [str(home)], 'forceReload': True})
        entry = result['data'][0]
        assert not entry['errors'], entry['errors']
        return {skill['name']: skill for skill in entry['skills'] if skill['enabled']}
    finally:
        signal.alarm(0)
        process.terminate()
        process.wait(timeout=10)

    from_plugins = {name for name in skills if ':' in name}
    assert from_plugins == expected_names, (from_plugins, expected_names)
    assert 'personal' in skills
    return skills

"""Inspect real Pi resources without authentication or a model request."""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

expected = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
expected_skills = {skill for skills in expected.values() for skill in skills}
agent_dir = Path.home() / '.pi/agent'
agent_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
settings = agent_dir / 'settings.json'
mcp = agent_dir / 'mcp.json'
user_server = {'url': 'http://127.0.0.1:9/personal', 'enabled': False}
user_settings = {'theme': 'light', 'defaultProvider': 'personal', 'defaultModel': 'personal-model',
                 'skills': []}
settings.write_text(json.dumps(user_settings))
mcp.write_text(json.dumps({'mcpServers': {'personal': user_server}, 'personalSetting': True}))
env = dict(os.environ, AGENT_DISTRO_SETTINGS='0', PI_OFFLINE='1')


def run(*args, launcher='pi', overrides=None, success=True):
    result = subprocess.run([launcher, *args], env=env | (overrides or {}),
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
    assert (result.returncode == 0) == success, (result.stdout, result.stderr)
    return result.stdout


def with_plugins(plugins):
    # AGENT_DISTRO_PLUGINS for one launch only.
    return {} if plugins is None else {'AGENT_DISTRO_PLUGINS': plugins}


def discover(launcher='pi', plugins=None, skills=None):
    want = expected_skills if skills is None else skills
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as cwd, tempfile.TemporaryFile() as output, tempfile.TemporaryFile() as errors:
        process = subprocess.Popen([launcher, '--no-session', '--mode', 'rpc'], cwd=cwd, env=env | with_plugins(plugins),
                                   stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=output, stderr=errors, text=True)
        try:
            process.stdin.write('{"type":"get_commands","id":"skills"}\n')
            process.stdin.flush()
            deadline = time.monotonic() + 120
            while time.monotonic() < deadline:
                data = os.pread(output.fileno(), os.fstat(output.fileno()).st_size, 0)
                messages = [json.loads(line) for line in data.splitlines(keepends=True)
                            if line.endswith(b'\n') and line.strip()]
                responses = [m for m in messages if m.get('command') == 'get_commands']
                if responses:
                    response = responses[0]
                    assert response['success'], response
                    commands = [c for c in response['data']['commands'] if c['source'] == 'skill']
                    assert {c['name'] for c in commands} == {'skill:' + s for s in want}, commands
                    for plugin, names in expected.items():
                        for name in names if skills is None else []:
                            assert any(c['sourceInfo']['path'].endswith(f'/{plugin}/{name}/SKILL.md')
                                       for c in commands), (plugin, name, commands)
                    return commands
                assert process.poll() is None, (process.returncode, data,
                    os.pread(errors.fileno(), os.fstat(errors.fileno()).st_size, 0))
                time.sleep(0.1)
            raise AssertionError(('RPC discovery timed out', messages))
        finally:
            process.terminate()
            process.communicate(timeout=10)


def inventory(launcher='pi', plugins=None):
    run('--version', launcher=launcher, overrides=with_plugins(plugins))
    resolved = json.loads(settings.read_text())
    for key, value in user_settings.items():
        if key != 'skills':
            assert resolved[key] == value, resolved
    servers = json.loads(mcp.read_text())
    assert servers['personalSetting'] is True
    assert servers['mcpServers']['personal'] == user_server
    if 'kolu' in expected:
        assert 'kolu' in servers['mcpServers'], servers
    if 'acme.spec-fixture' in expected:
        assert {'placeholders', 'explicit-cwd', 'data-cwd', 'remote'} <= servers['mcpServers'].keys()
        assert 'invalid' not in servers['mcpServers']
        assert servers['mcpServers']['remote'] == {
            'url': 'http://127.0.0.1:9/mcp', 'headers': {'X-Tenant': 'fixture'}}
    return resolved, servers

# Builds the website (./doc) and publishes it to GitHub Pages.
# The custom domain is set in the repository's Pages settings.
name: Pages

on:
  # Pages serves one site, built from main. A docs change on a PR branch is
  # checked by odu's `site` recipe; the `github-pages` environment only
  # deploys main, so other branches would just fail the deploy.
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "doc/**"
      - ".github/workflows/pages.yaml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - uses: cachix/install-nix-action@13d8dd58da0234aa297dedd986986ccb8e7f3e24 # v31
        with:
          github_access_token: ${{ github.token }}
          extra_nix_config: |
            extra-substituters = https://cache.nixos.asia/oss
            extra-trusted-public-keys = oss:KO872wNJkCDgmGN3xy9dT89WAhvv13EiKncTtHDItVU=

      - run: nix build ./doc -L -o ./_site

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@56afc609e74202658d3ffba0e8f6dda462b719fa # v3

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@d6db90164ac5ed86f2b6aed7e0febac5b3c0c03e # v4

name: Update Flake

on:
  schedule:
    # modules/home-manager.nix defaults to 02:00, 08:00, 14:00, 20:00 UTC, two
    # hours after each run of this job.
    # Keep that default aligned when changing this upstream schedule.
    - cron: '0 */6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Runs share the update branch and pull request, so they must not overlap.
concurrency: update-flake

jobs:
  update:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      # Approve the runs this job's pull request is waiting on.
      actions: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - uses: cachix/install-nix-action@13d8dd58da0234aa297dedd986986ccb8e7f3e24 # v31
        with:
          github_access_token: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Read the pinned package versions
        id: versions-before
        run: |
          versions=$(bash .github/scripts/read-versions.sh)
          pins=$(python3 .github/scripts/read-pins.py)
          echo "versions=$versions" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "pins=$pins" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Advance directory-local sources
        run: bash .github/scripts/update-sources.sh

      - name: Update the root lock
        id: lock
        shell: bash
        run: |
          nix flake update --log-format raw 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/flake-update.log"
          versions=$(bash .github/scripts/read-versions.sh)
          echo "versions=$versions" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          pins=$(python3 .github/scripts/read-pins.py)
          metadata=$(nix eval --json .#harnessMeta --apply "meta: meta (builtins.fromJSON ''$versions'')")
          echo "pins=$pins" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "metadata=$metadata" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Update the sub-flake locks after the root lock
        run: bash test/update-lock.sh

      - name: Describe the locked versions
        id: report
        env:
          VERSIONS_BEFORE: ${{ steps.versions-before.outputs.versions }}
          VERSIONS_AFTER: ${{ steps.lock.outputs.versions }}
          HARNESS_META: ${{ steps.lock.outputs.metadata }}
          PINS_BEFORE: ${{ steps.versions-before.outputs.pins }}
          PINS_AFTER: ${{ steps.lock.outputs.pins }}
        run: python3 .github/scripts/describe-flake-update.py

      - uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@5f6978faf089d4d20b00c7766989d076bb2fc7f1 # v8
        id: update
        with:
          branch: flake-update
          delete-branch: true
          add-paths: |
            flake.nix
            flake.lock
            test/flake.lock
            doc/flake.lock
            harnesses
            lib/npins
          title: ${{ steps.report.outputs.pr-title }}
          body-path: ${{ steps.report.outputs.pr-body-path }}
          commit-message: "chore(flake): update inputs"
          labels: dependencies

      # A pull request that GITHUB_TOKEN opens leaves its workflow runs waiting
      # for a maintainer to approve them, and quiet wording in the checks UI
      # hides that they never ran. This job created the pull request, so it
      # approves those runs itself instead of asking a maintainer to start the
      # same builds every morning. What the runs then prove is unchanged: the
      # `build (…)` and `publish (…)` contexts `cache.yml` posts are required by
      # `Require CI on main`, and they report on the commit this pull request
      # merges.
      - name: Approve the runs the update pull request is waiting on
        if: steps.update.outputs.pull-request-number != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR: ${{ steps.update.outputs.pull-request-number }}
        run: |
          sha=$(gh pr view "$PR" --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)
          approved=0
          for _ in $(seq 20); do
            pending=$(gh run list --commit "$sha" --limit 50 --json databaseId,status,conclusion \
              --jq '[.[] | select(.status == "action_required" or .conclusion == "action_required")
                     | .databaseId] | join(" ")')
            if [ -n "$pending" ]; then
              for run in $pending; do
                echo "Approving run $run"
                gh api -X POST "repos/$GH_REPO/actions/runs/$run/approve" >/dev/null
              done
              approved=$((approved + 1))
            elif [ "$approved" -gt 0 ]; then
              break
            fi
            sleep 10
          done

      # Enable auto-merge and stop there: the ruleset gates the merge, so no
      # job here has to watch the checks. What it waits on is odu's
      # `<recipe>@<platform>` statuses — posted by whoever runs odu on this
      # pull request, which is how this repository's CI reports now — plus the
      # `build (…)` and `publish (…)` contexts of `cache.yml`, whose runs the
      # step above just approved. GitHub merges the moment they are all green.
      - name: Merge once the required checks are green
        if: steps.update.outputs.pull-request-number != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR: ${{ steps.update.outputs.pull-request-number }}
        run: gh pr merge --squash --auto --delete-branch "$PR"

# agent-distro **Your team's coding agents, in one command.** Package your skills, MCP servers, and harness settings once, and run them in every harness. ```sh nix run github:juspay/agent-distro ``` Installs keep themselves up to date from the project's binary cache and never compile. A Linux machine whose Nix will not trust that cache — a shared host where you are not a trusted user — updates too, from the content-addressed store paths published for every revision (built with Nix 2.34.x: Nix 2.35 changed how a self-referential path is addressed, and a host on it cannot take them); a Mac needs the cache key or a trusted user, because a rewritten Mach-O does not run on arm64 macOS. Everything else is on the website, ****: - [Quick start](https://agent-distro.nixos.asia/#quick-start) - [Install and keep updated](https://agent-distro.nixos.asia/#install) - [The binary cache](https://agent-distro.nixos.asia/#binary-cache) - [Package layout](https://agent-distro.nixos.asia/#package-layout) - [Profiles](https://agent-distro.nixos.asia/#profiles) - [Harnesses](https://agent-distro.nixos.asia/#harnesses) - [How it works](https://agent-distro.nixos.asia/#how-it-works) - [Development](https://agent-distro.nixos.asia/#development) - [Adding a harness](https://agent-distro.nixos.asia/#adding-a-harness)

# Pi

Merges plugin MCP servers and materialized skill paths into its user
JSON files, preserving personal entries, auth, and sessions. A profile's
`env` is exported before Pi starts, and a `secret` variable it declares is
prompted for when it is not already set. Every profile defaults
`hideThinkingBlock` to `true`; set it to `false` in `settings.json` to show
thinking blocks again. Pi has no `settings.<harness>` of a profile to read:
its own files are where its providers live.

Each stdio MCP server runs through a generated launcher, in the directory the
harness was launched in (doc/index.md, "Working directory"). A plugin on
`AGENT_DISTRO_PLUGINS` is merged the same way, but for one launch:
the merge records what it added in `.agent-distro-launch.json` in the agent
directory, and the next merge removes
whatever is still as recorded before applying its own, so the entries stay
until the next `pi` launch, however much later that is. Without a home for
those files (`HOME` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` unset, or a directory it cannot
write), the launch fails rather than start without the plugins. Launches that run at
the same moment with different values can see each other's entries, since Pi
reads them from the same files. A profile read at launch (an
`agent-distro.nix`) is merged as these are.

The npins branch pin tracks `sadjow/pi-nix`. Its standalone binary packaging
recipe is called with the distribution's shared nixpkgs rather than the
packaging repo's own pin.

# OMP

Passes plugins as `-e` roots, composing with user extensions. A plugin on
`AGENT_DISTRO_PLUGINS` is validated and passed as one more `-e` root, its own
directory, replacing a plugin of a profile in effect that has the same name. A
profile read at launch (an `agent-distro.nix`) reaches OMP the same way. Its stdio MCP servers run through a generated launcher, in the directory the
launch was typed in (doc/index.md, "Working directory"). The environment and
the `settings.omp` of the profile in effect, read at launch, are exported
before OMP starts — a `secret` variable is prompted for when it is not already
set — and its YAML fills only the keys the user has not set, preserving
existing values and comments. Every profile fills `hideThinkingBlock: true`
and `task.showResolvedModelBadge: true`, so thinking blocks stay hidden and a
subagent's row names the model it resolved to; set either to `false` in
`config.yml` to turn it off again.

OMP uses an npins release pin. Its source build is loaded from upstream's lock,
except that every nixpkgs in it is the distribution's shared nixpkgs.

# Claude Code

Writes each plugin as a self-contained Claude Code plugin
root, passed with `--plugin-dir` for that session: its manifest, its
discovered skills, and a `.mcp.json`. Each stdio MCP server runs through a
generated launcher that provides `PLUGIN_ROOT`, `PLUGIN_DATA`, placeholder
expansion and the working directory (doc/index.md, "Working directory").
Extra user plugins compose with them; no persistent installation is needed.

A plugin on `AGENT_DISTRO_PLUGINS` is written the same way into the cache and
added as one more `--plugin-dir`; one named like a plugin of a profile in
effect takes its place. Like the profile's, it lasts only for the session. A
profile read at launch (an `agent-distro.nix`) is written the same way, its
plugins ahead of the variable's.

The npins branch pin tracks `sadjow/claude-code-nix`. Its standalone binary
packaging recipe is called with the distribution's shared nixpkgs, which allows
unfree packages, rather than the packaging repo's own pin.
